target: AWS Random Cut Forest: ThresholdedRandomCutForest thresholder (BasicThresholder via PredictorCorrector)
version: Java 4.4.0 (HEAD Java main sources identical to tag 4.4.0-java); Rust crate 4.0.0
licence_notes: No restriction on reading, running, benchmarking or publishing.
adoption: 242 GitHub stars, 36 forks (GitHub API 2026-11-11); embedded by OpenSearch Anomaly Detection (build.gradle:164 of opensearch-ad pins parkservices 4.4.0).
scope_reason: Installable library (Maven Central, crates.io); with builder defaults the threshold changes with every score.
default_path: ThresholdedRandomCutForest.builder() defaults (ThresholdedRandomCutForest.java:676-711: sampleSize 256, 50 trees, shingleSize 1, anomalyRate 0.01, transformMethod NONE, autoAdjust false, zFactor 3, alertOnce false; timeDecay 1/2560 from RandomCutForest.java:356) -> process() -> augment() (ThresholdedRandomCutForest.java:216-224) -> PredictorCorrector.detect() sets anomalyGrade (PredictorCorrector.java:950); alarm = grade > 0.
update_rule: Discounted mean and deviation of the RCF score; threshold = max(absolute floor 0.8, mean + ((factor-1)*longTermDeviation + primaryDeviation)), factor = max(3, 2.0 floor) (BasicThresholder.java:258-271).
learning_region: all scored points, flagged or not; raw score clamped at 2.0 before entering the primary statistic

evidence.quote: result.setAnomalyGrade(workingGrade);

default_when_configurable: not configurable: no API withholds a point from saveScores
memory: Primary Deviation discount = forest timeDecay = 1/2560 per score (~2560-score exponential window, inferred from Deviation.update); secondary deviation discount = anomalyRate 0.01 (~100 scores); thresholdDeviation discount timeDecay/2.
direction_bounds: Symmetric. Input clamp min(score, 2.0) on the primary statistic. Absolute floor 0.8 (setAbsoluteThreshold, ThresholdedRandomCutForest.java:142-145, autoAdjust false). Factor floor 2.0. Initial threshold 1.5 for first 10 scores, blended to adaptive by 20. For shingle 1 / no differencing the deviation term is min(sqrt2*thresholdDeviation, primaryDeviation) and thresholdDeviation learns only gaps below the mean (Java; Rust learns gaps above the mean).
alarm_logic: Grade > 0 alarms immediately; no on-delay or consecutive count. Correction filters can zero the grade: noise test, ANOMALY_IN_SHINGLE, FORECAST (ignoreNearExpected box); with autoAdjust (off by default) CONDITIONAL_FORECAST and DATA_DRIFT; with alertOnce (off by default) ALERT_ONCE. Filtered points still update the thresholder.
operator_controls: lowerThreshold (absolute floor), zFactor, ignoreNearExpected{From,}{Above,Below}{,ByRatio}, autoAdjust, alertOnce, scoreDifferencing, initialThreshold. No freeze, no exclusion window, no feedback labels.
documentation_quote: silent on anomalies entering the threshold. Code comment PredictorCorrector.java:779-780: "a consequence of this can be masking -- anomalies just after a run/drift would be difficult to determine".
differs: EWMA mean + k deviations including alarms, but with a 2.0 input clamp, a 0.8 absolute floor, and a deviation term partly learned only from scores below the mean.

predictions.sustained: absorb (prediction): mean rises with clamped attack scores, and the forest (separate row) lowers the scores themselves.
predictions.loud: resist, weakly (prediction): 2.0 clamp and 1/2560 discount bound each pulse's pull on the mean.
predictions.frog: absorb (prediction): sub-threshold scores enter the mean at full weight with no hold-out.
predictions.subl: unclear (prediction): no minimum alarm duration and no alarm exclusion, so the campaign premise does not apply; short pulses alarm and enter like loud pulses.

runnable: In-process: Java jar (JVM, <1 GB for one series) or Rust crate. Feasible on 16 GB laptop.
notes: Rust port: same unconditional update and 2.0 clamp (basicthresholder.rs:217-219), but update_threshold uses score - mean (gaps above mean) where Java uses mean - score (BasicThresholder.java:309); Rust default forest time decay 0.1/capacity (basictrcf.rs:307). Python wrapper calls Java via JPype.
unresolved: Intent of passing anomalyRate as the secondary deviation discount (PredictorCorrector.java:122) unclear.

target: AWS Random Cut Forest: forest model (time-decayed reservoir sample per tree) under ThresholdedRandomCutForest

adoption: 242 GitHub stars, 36 forks (GitHub API 2026-11-11); embedded by OpenSearch AD.

default_path: ThresholdedRandomCutForest.process() -> augment() -> postProcess() -> preprocessor.update(..., forest) -> forest.update(point).
update_rule: Each tree's sampler admits the point with a time-decayed random priority (weight -(t)*timeDecay + log(-log(U)/w), w = 1.0) and evicts the max-priority point; tree updated accordingly.
learning_region: all points, flagged or not, at sampling weight 1.0

evidence.quote:

operator_controls: timeDecay, sampleSize, initialAcceptFraction. No exclusion of flagged points.
documentation_quote: Java/README.md:97: "By default, we set `timeDecay` equal to `1 / (10 * sampleSize)`." Silent on anomalies entering the sample.
differs: A model retrained continuously on a decaying sample that includes flagged points; no tt1 rule models the score generator.

predictions.loud: resist, weakly (prediction): few pulse points in a 256-point sample; pulses remain isolated in the trees.

target: Elastic ML (ml-cpp): per-series time-series model (priors, trend decomposition, change-point handling)
version: main 9.7.0 (gradle.properties / version.properties); latest GitHub release v9.5.6
licence: Elastic License 2.0 plus additional limitation (ml-cpp/LICENSE.txt:1-8); elasticsearch x-pack ML files ELv2-only
licence_notes: ELv2 permits use, copy, distribution, derivative works; forbids hosted service, licence-key circumvention, notice removal. Additional limitation: ML functionality 'may only be used in production when invoked by an Elasticsearch process with a license key installed that permits use of machine learning features'. Anomaly-detection jobs need PLATINUM (MachineLearning.java:517-521); self-generated trial 30 days (LicenseSettings.java:41). ELv2 and repos are silent on benchmarking and publishing results; Elastic EULA / trial terms not read: unclear.
adoption: ml-cpp 158 GitHub stars, 68 forks (GitHub API 2026-11-11); shipped in every default Elasticsearch distribution.
scope_reason: Licence permits reading; installable product; model updates every bucket by default.
default_path: Anomaly detection job, single metric detector, default settings: CMetricModel::sample -> CUnivariateTimeSeriesModel::countWeights (outlier weight) -> addSamples; probability -> raw score -> normaliser (separate row). Alarm decided outside ml-cpp (Kibana rule / watch on normalised score; default not read).
update_rule: Bayesian prior and decomposition update with count weight multiplied by an outlier weight: 1 for model p >= 1e-3, log-interpolated to a minimum at p <= 1e-5; minimum = 0.01 + 0.49*derate, derate 1 -> 0 over the first 3 weeks of a series and over 3 days after a change point. Level shifts lasting >= max(30 h, 5 window buckets) are applied as change points.
learning_region: all buckets; improbable values at reduced weight (0.01-0.5, never 0); sustained shifts adopted via change-point test
default_when_configurable: Outlier down-weighting always on; skip_model_update rules and calendar events (operator) can exclude buckets, none by default.
memory: Decay 0.0005 per standard 30-min bucket, scaled by bucket length (CAnomalyDetectorModelConfig.cc:64, 111-112); trend decay min(48*decay/..., 0.1) (lines 155-160). Half-life in hours not derived.
direction_bounds: Outlier weight floor 0.01 (0.5 early in a series or after a change); change-point minimum length max(30 h, 5 window buckets), doubled for sparse data (CTimeSeriesDecompositionDetail.cc:923-936); changes can be undone if the series reverts (874-902).
alarm_logic: None in ml-cpp; probability -> raw score -> normalised score. Kibana rule default not read.
operator_controls: Custom rules (skip_result, skip_model_update), calendars/scheduled events (weight 0, CAnomalyDetectorModel.cc:489-493), model snapshots/revert (not read).
documentation_quote: silent in ml-cpp (docs/ holds changelogs only; CHANGELOG.asciidoc:283 'Better handling of outliers in update immediately after detecting changes in time'). Elastic docs site not read.
differs: Soft exclusion (weight down to 0.01, never 0) keyed on the model's own tail p-value, plus a change detector that adopts shifts lasting >= 30 h; not a threshold on a score.

predictions.sustained: absorb (prediction): change-point test adopts the shift after ~30 h; before that weight 0.01 slows learning.
predictions.loud: resist (prediction): pulses with p <= 1e-5 enter at ~0.01 weight once the series is >3 weeks old.
predictions.frog: absorb (prediction): values with p >= 1e-3 enter at full weight.
predictions.subl: unclear (prediction): bucket aggregation function and span decide what the model sees.

runnable: Docker docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch single node x86_64 with 30-day trial; ~4-6 GB estimated; feasible on 16 GB. Publishing results: licence terms unclear.
notes: The outlier-weight p-value is the model's tail probability of the detrended value; related to, but not identical with, the record score users alarm on (inferred).
unresolved: Mapping from outlier-weight p-value to the scores users alarm on; role of CTimeSeriesAnomalyModel during long anomalies; Kibana defaults (bucket_span, alert severity).

target: Elastic ML (ml-cpp + x-pack): anomaly score normaliser and renormalisation
licence: Elastic License 2.0 plus additional limitation (ml-cpp); ELv2-only (x-pack)
licence_notes: As model row. Running needs Platinum or 30-day trial; benchmarking/publishing terms unclear.
scope_reason: The normalised 0-100 score is what users threshold; its mapping adapts with every bucket.
default_path: CHierarchicalResultsNormalizer (E_UpdateQuantiles) -> CAnomalyScore::CNormalizer::updateQuantiles(scope, score); normalised score from quantile -> knot points (0,0),(70,1),(85,1.2),(90,1.5),(95,3),(97,20),(99,50),(99.9,90),(100,100). Java ScoresUpdater rewrites past results when quantiles change.
update_rule: Raw score (0 if probability > 0.035, else anomalyScore(p)) maxed over m_CountPerSample buckets, discretised, added to a 201-node q-digest plus a high-quantile summary above the 90th percentile; quantiles aged every 20 sample periods.
learning_region: all bucket raw scores, unless skip_model_update rule or scheduled event applies
default_when_configurable: Default: all scores enter. Configurable per detector via skip_model_update rules or calendars (operator, none by default).
memory: q-digest decays at the job decay rate but only every QUANTILE_DECAY_TIME = 20 sample periods (CAnomalyScore.h:236; CAnomalyScore.cc:681-705); renormalisation window max(30 days, 100 buckets).
direction_bounds: Normalised score in [0, 100]; raw score 0 for probability > 0.035 (CAnomalyDetectorModelConfig.cc:89).
alarm_logic: None in ml-cpp; renormalisation can lower past scores retroactively. Kibana rule default not read.
documentation_quote: silent in ml-cpp; code comment CAnomalyScore.cc:687-689: 'Quantiles age at a much slower rate than everything else so that we can accurately estimate high quantiles.' Elastic docs site not read.
differs: Quantile of past scores including alarms, but over a long slowly-decaying history rather than one day, and applied retroactively to the last 30 days.

predictions.sustained: absorb (prediction): attack raw scores fill upper quantiles; current and renormalised past scores fall.
predictions.loud: absorb (prediction): each pulse adds a high raw score; slow decay lets them accumulate.
predictions.frog: unclear (prediction): raw score is 0 above probability 0.035, so a frog below that line leaves the normaliser untouched; above it, it adds scores.

notes: m_CountPerSample = HOUR / clamp(2*bucketLength, 5 min, 1 h) buckets per sample (CAnomalyScore.cc:257-260).
unresolved: Kibana alert severity default; size of renormalisation effect not derived.
